sections.text: Neil Young filed a ten-million-dollar copyright infringement lawsuit against Donald Trump's fundraising committee, the Trump 47 Committee. Young previously sued Trump's re-election campaign in 2020 over the same song, which was settled.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: An Egyptian court convicted Mada Masr editor-in-chief Lina Attalah of managing an unlicensed website. The judge ordered the site's closure and a 3m Egyptian pounds fine. sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Human rights groups and press freedom watchdogs condemned the ruling as a major blow to independent media in Egypt. The Committee to Protect Journalists and Amnesty International warned that the verdict threatens remaining critical reporting in the country.

sections.text: An anonymous celebrity known as PPT asked the High Court to prevent ITN and Guardian News and Media from publishing allegations of inappropriate sexual activities. sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Artificial intelligence bots submitted tens of thousands of fake responses to a government consultation regarding the ban on disposable vapes in 2023. Authorities identified that seventy-six percent of the total submissions were machine-generated and opposed the proposed ban.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Researchers note this is likely the first recorded instance of large-scale automated interference in UK public health policymaking. Such incidents threaten to distort public consultations and make corporate interests appear as popular public movements.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The government successfully excluded the automated submissions from its decision-making and passed the legislation into law. Officials and experts emphasize the need for continued vigilance and better screening against future technological interference.

gist: Amy-Jane Beer gathered water from the Gypsey Race for a river rights charter.
Collaborators blended waters from across Yorkshire to create ink for the charter ceremony.
Participants swam at the confluence of the Ouse and Foss before the ceremony.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Amy-Jane Beer visited the Gypsey Race stream in Yorkshire to request permission to collect water. She helped organise a gathering of river advocates co-drafting a regional charter of river rights. Water collected from various Yorkshire rivers, becks and springs was blended during a ceremony to make ink for writing the charter. Before the event, collaborators swam at the confluence of the Ouse and Foss.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The Gypsey Race stream is associated with local folklore and prehistoric sites, including barrows, henges and England's tallest standing stone. Its flow is locally believed to hold the power of prophecy. The gathering aimed to make explicit people's responsibilities towards rivers through the charter.

sections.text: A new study indicates that annual new dementia cases globally will more than double by 2050, while US diagnoses are projected to rise significantly. gist: Political activist Tommy Robinson was found guilty of harassing two Daily Mail journalists.
He targeted reporters Andrew Young and Jacob Dirnhuber after the newspaper reported on his Cyprus holiday.
Robinson faces up to 10 years in prison and awaits sentencing on 16 December.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Tommy Robinson was convicted of two counts of harassment causing fear of violence at Southwark Crown Court. He targeted journalists Andrew Young and Jacob Dirnhuber following a Daily Mail article about him in Cyprus. Robinson posted personal details online, hired private investigators, and made threatening calls.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The prosecution stated that Robinson weaponised social media. The journalists and their families were forced to flee their homes and employ private security due to safety fears.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Robinson was granted bail and is scheduled to be sentenced on 16 December. He faces a maximum sentence of 10 years in prison.

fivew: Political activist Tommy Robinson, also known as Stephen Yaxley-Lennon.

The verdict was delivered in December following a trial at Southwark Crown Court.
He retaliated against reporters who published a story about him being in Cyprus during riots in England.

Huerta co-founded the United Farm Workers union and coined the phrase 'Sí, se puede!'.
Her family announced her death, with plans to celebrate her life to follow.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Dolores Huerta, a pioneering civil rights activist and labour organiser, died in California on Wednesday aged 96. The BBC confirmed she died of cancer.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Huerta co-founded the United Farm Workers union with Cesar Chavez, securing landmark contracts, overtime pay, and protections against heat deaths for agricultural labourers. She coined the rallying cry 'Sí, se puede!', helped negotiate immigration reforms, and championed women's and voting rights across several decades.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Huerta's family announced they will follow up on plans to recognise and celebrate her life and legacy.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Prime Minister Andy Burnham ruled out calling a general election in the next 12 months. Opposition leaders Kemi Badenoch and Nigel Farage had claimed Burnham would hold an early vote. Burnham also told cabinet ministers not to express personal opinions on future EU relations.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Opposition figures argued Burnham lacks a mandate after becoming prime minister following Sir Keir Starmer's resignation. Burnham countered that the Conservative Brexit deal caused low growth, but insisted government policy on EU relations must remain disciplined during this parliamentary term.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Burnham will attend a European summit next month to discuss initial Brexit changes within manifesto limits. Any major alterations to the UK's relationship with the EU will form part of a 10-year plan for the public to decide after the next election.

sections.text: The Chancellor unveiled a safe Budget with limited help for households impacted by energy and fuel bills. The tax burden is set to rise to a historic high of 38.6%, driven by frozen tax thresholds.

sections.heading: What happens next

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Microsoft posted first-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue of $92.3 billion and net income of $33.6 billion. For the first time, Microsoft disclosed quarterly Azure dollar revenue, reporting $33.17 billion according to The Verge, or $33.2 billion according to TechCrunch. sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: A group calling itself the Department of Peace accessed and leaked details of over 41,000 Department of Homeland Security personnel. Distributed Denial of Secrets published the database, named Icepick. Outlets disagree on exact numbers for Immigration and Customs Enforcement, citing nearly 6,600, about 6,600, 7,000, or roughly 10,000 records. sections.heading: Why it matters

It follows controversial immigration crackdowns, fatal shootings by agents, and official efforts to conceal staff identities while seeking to unmask public critics.

sections.heading: What happens next

timeline.text: Building boom puts 300,000 people in the path of potential Himalayan disasters

gist: Built-up land in high-risk Himalayan zones grew by about 45% between 2016 and 2023.
At least 300,000 people now live in the path of potential Himalayan disasters.
Rapid warming speeds up glacier melting, destabilising slopes and expanding glacial lakes.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: A new study reveals that built-up land in high-risk zones across northern Nepal, Tibet, and India's Uttarakhand increased by roughly 45% between 2016 and 2023. Areas threatened by glacial lake flooding saw development rise by almost 78%. Tourism facilities, real estate, and infrastructure expanded rapidly along river banks and trekking regions.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Warming in the Himalayas occurs at twice the global rate, accelerating glacier melt and destabilising mountain slopes. This increases the risk of catastrophic floods and landslides, threatening at least 300,000 people. Campaigners note that building regulations are poorly enforced and development has occurred without proper planning.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Authorities in Nepal plan to ban settlements within 15m of riverbanks along specific corridors, and Uttarakhand approved new floodplain zoning rules. However, experts warn that mitigating threats completely will remain a major challenge.

fivew: Researchers from the UK, Nepal, and India.
A study found significant development growth in high-risk Himalayan disaster zones.
Northern Nepal, south-eastern Tibet, and Uttarakhand in India.
Tourism, housing, and infrastructure expansion have outpaced safety planning amid regional warming.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Ofcom recommended four age verification methods ahead of the UK's social media ban for under-16s, starting next March. sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Under-16s will be blocked from ten major platforms, including Instagram, TikTok and Snapchat. Age checks are difficult because teenagers often lack credit cards or passports. Child safety groups stressed that tech firms must be held accountable to prevent children from bypassing the rules, as occurred in Australia.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The government will consider Ofcom's report and decide by the end of the year. Tech providers must establish compliant age verification before the March deadline.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Microsoft offered voluntary buyouts to approximately 60,000 employees across multiple regions to lower operating costs and support AI infrastructure investments. Meanwhile, Denmark ended its trial moving away from Microsoft Office after encountering formatting and tracking issues. In gaming and leadership, Xbox executives departed, and Microsoft merged its Forza developers.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The workforce reductions signal how artificial intelligence is fundamentally changing Microsoft's staffing needs and operating costs. Additionally, Denmark's return to Microsoft software highlights the ongoing reliance on established US tech vendors despite efforts to diversify.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Dónal Lunny, a prominent multi-instrumentalist, arranger and producer in Irish traditional music, died of cancer at the age of 79. He was known for playing the guitar, keyboards and bodhrán, and for popularising the Irish bouzouki. Throughout his career, he played in major folk bands including Planxty, the Bothy Band and Moving Hearts, and collaborated with numerous artists.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Lunny played a vital role in shaping traditional Irish music by developing new harmonic and rhythmic structures and forming highly influential groups. His work spanned successful band recordings, production, film and television composition, and cross-genre collaborations with prominent international artists.

gist: Russell Brand gave evidence at his trial, denying all charges.
He stated that allegations and documentaries caused severe personal and professional impact.
The trial at Southwark Crown Court continues.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Russell Brand took the witness stand at Southwark Crown Court. He denied multiple charges of sexual offences involving six complainants across a decade. During questioning by his defence barrister, Brand stated that consent is essential and denied committing any of the alleged acts.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The entertainer testified that publicity surrounding the claims affected his life and relationships deeply. He described losing support from peers and being barred from a hospital where his child underwent surgery.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The legal proceedings at Southwark Crown Court are ongoing as the trial continues.

fivew: Russell Brand gave evidence denying several sexual offence charges at his trial.
To present his defence against allegations spanning between 1999 and 2009.

timeline.text: 'Relax, I love Kane and Lamine Yamal' - Henry defends his Ballon d'Or hosting

gist: Thierry Henry defended his Ballon d'Or ceremony hosting after facing criticism over remarks.
He addressed jokes made towards Lamine Yamal, co-host Kate Scott, and winner Harry Kane.
Henry stated people were getting excited about nothing and emphasised his admiration for the players.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Thierry Henry hosted the Ballon d'Or ceremony alongside Kate Scott. He faced criticism for remarks made towards Lamine Yamal regarding his young player award, for correcting Scott's pronunciation of Socrates, and for admitting he wanted Kylian Mbappe to win the top prize over Harry Kane.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Henry's comments drew an audible reaction from the audience and subsequent criticism on social media, leading him to release a video defending his actions and clarifying his intentions.

sections.heading: What happens next

The League Two team advanced by defeating Arsenal in a penalty shootout.
The quarter-final matches are scheduled for the week starting 14 December.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Fleetwood Town advanced to the quarter-finals after overcoming Arsenal on penalties. They will now face the winners of the match between Everton and Newcastle United. Meanwhile, holders Manchester City were drawn against Bradford City, Liverpool will play Bournemouth, and Crystal Palace face Sunderland.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Fleetwood Town are the lowest-ranked club remaining in the tournament and have achieved a historic milestone by reaching the final eight.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Fleetwood await the conclusion of the fourth-round fixture between Everton and Newcastle to discover their specific opponent. The quarter-final ties are scheduled to occur during the week beginning 14 December.

gist: Harry Kane won the Ballon d'Or at the London Palladium.
His career included challenging loan spells at Leyton Orient, Millwall, Norwich City, and Leicester City.
He achieved success at Tottenham Hotspur, Bayern Munich, and for England.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Harry Kane won the Ballon d'Or at the London Palladium, beating Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal. His career included loan spells at lower division clubs before breaking through at Tottenham Hotspur and later moving to Bayern Munich.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: He became the first English player to win the trophy since 2001 and the fifth overall, proving his doubters wrong through hard work and dedication.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: After celebrations, Kane returns to business with Bayern Munich playing Magdeburg and Borussia Dortmund, while targeting potential success with England at Euro 2028.

fivew: Harry Kane won the Ballon d'Or.
His exemplary career and goalscoring success for club and country.

quotes.text: Work hard in silence. Let success be your noise.
